long_description:
Playtime for serious professionals.

A free community event where we get together, talk creativity and doodle around.

Our theme this month is Adventure. We'll talk about the power of exploration and experimentation, and design creative adventures we can take ourselves on over the summer break.

It's also our final session for 2026 and we'll be hanging out and celebrating the first year of Doodle Cafe!

This event is in-person at Cuckoo Emporium, 57 Customhouse Quay in Pōneke/Wellington.

What to expect?

a fun, low-stakes, judgement-free zone where we exercise our imagination muscles

the warmth of other people's creative energy

hands-on doodling time, with prompts and support to work through creative blocks

What to bring?

a notebook

pens/pencils/whatever you’d like to work with

your curiosity

(optional) specific ideas and questions you want to doodle around with — work-related or otherwise

No drawing skills required.

Doodle Cafe is free, but spaces are limited. Grab your ticket today and invite your friends and colleagues.

We're generously hosted by the awesome team at Cuckoo — so enjoy the space and grab drinks and snacks on the night.

—————————

Hi! I'm Kate, a former lawyer, artist and creativity coach. I help serious professionals get seriously creative, through corporate workshops and 1:1 coaching. Learn more about my work at www.jointherenaissance.org.

id: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking-10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

long_description:
Two behaviour change disciplines walk into a bar...

The NZ Social Marketing Network and the Behavioural Insights Community of Practice are coming together for an informal end-of-year event to explore what social marketers and behavioural scientists actually do, where our worlds overlap, and how we can work better together.

Hear from practitioners across both disciplines as they share a glimpse into their day-to-day work, the challenges they tackle, and the approaches to tackling behaviour change challenges.

Then join the conversation about where we can learn from each other, spark new ideas and collaborate.

And because it's nearly Christmas, we'll wrap things up with festive drinks and good chats 🎄


We’ll kick off with some casual presentations at 4pm, followed by Q&A and table discussions, before wrapping up the formalities by 5pm and moving into Christmas drinks and chats!

Please RSVP so we can keep track of numbers, feel free to invite others that are interested in behaviour change.

name: Shut Up & Dance for Nala: A Fundraiser Supporting A Family Through Cancer Treatments
venue: 11 Ganges Road, Khandallah, Wellington 6035, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special Shut Up & Dance class as we come together to support one of our own!

Beautiful four-year-old Nala, daughter of our dance community member Mil, has been diagnosed with a rare childhood cancer. As Nala and her family navigate treatment and the difficult and uncertain road ahead, we want to surround them with love and support in a way we know how: by dancing together.

Shut Up & Dance is generously partnering with us for this special fundraiser class, with all funds raised after event costs going directly to Nala’s family to help ease some of the practical and financial pressures that come with caring for a seriously ill child.

Come dance, sweat, laugh, and move with us — for Nala, for Mil and her family, and for the community that shows up for each other when it matters most.

No dance experience needed. Just come as you are and dance for Nala 💛

long_description:
Immerse yourself in a breathtaking 3-hour cinematic journey into the world’s most spectacular marine environments. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour brings together an extraordinary collection of short films celebrating the beauty, power and wonder of our oceans.

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. Meet the passionate divers, fearless surfers, dedicated ocean advocates, ocean explorers and marine scientists whose lives are shaped by their connection to the sea.

Featuring spectacular underwater cinematography, heart-stopping ocean adventures and intimate stories of the people who dedicate their lives to exploring and protecting our oceans, every film offers a fresh perspective on the world beneath the waves.

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.

The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power. Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

Find out more at https://oceanfilmfestivalworldtour.com/tickets-new-zealand/

 

The Ocean Film Festival is exempt from Classification, but all swearing has been beeped out.

Recommended age 10+

 

SORRY NO REFUNDS : SEATING IS NOT ALLOCATED.

ONE SCREENING ONLY

Photo credit: Jake Wilton

 

Presented by Adventure Reels

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout.

long_description:
"Every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings" — Zuzu, It’s a Wonderful Life

Dementia Wellington invites you to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Frank Capra's inspiring Christmas classic It’s a Wonderful Life with your whānau and friends in the lavish Embassy Theatre.

Proceeds from this event will help Dementia Wellington provide community-based specialised support services for those experiencing dementia across the wider Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington area.

A fundraising afternoon tea will be served from 2:30pm. Seasonal, Tiered Cake Stands containing goodies and treats can be purchased to take into the Movie for sharing and enjoying. Your stand will be disassembled, wrapped and bagged for you to take home.

After the movie, a symbol of hope made by one of our Dementia Friends – a "Zuzu's Rose Petal" – will be available for you to take home as well. You are welcome to make a petal yourself to leave for someone else.

"My thanks go to you, young and old, for supporting Dementia Wellington with our work. Your generosity, as always, makes such a difference. Our team looks forward to seeing you on 13 December at this celebrated Christmas holiday tradition. My very best wishes."

Stephanie Clare, Chief Executive, Dementia Wellington

We look forward to enjoying this very special film with you and your loved ones this December in support of Dementia Wellington and encourage you to spread the word!

Tickets can also be acquired on the day.


If you would like to check out a little more about the man spearheading the whole event, check out this interview!

long_description:
Ministry of House is back in Session at Superfina!

Saturday December 5th from 9pm - 2am.

Join us for the last time in 2026 as we celebrate Crooked Mind’s birthday.

Banging margaritas from the team at Superfina will be on as per usual!

Ben-Jammin is kicking things off with his signature funky jams, while Crooked Mind will be taking you for a ride with his exclusive UKG takeover set to celebrate another lap around the sun.

Joining Ministry of House for the evening is their friend Joe, better known as PocketLipps.

PocketLipps, a Welly-based selector with over two decades behind the decks, is driven by a lifelong obsession with sound. From his early days in Nelson's river-valley raves to serving up a slew of original edits and productions to peak-time slots at Taniwha’s Denfestival, a sold-out sweat pit at Morning People, & jams with the S-Ence,  Breakaway, & High Functioning crews, he’s a master of crafting fluid, unexpected journeys. Expect a seamless blend of funky, gritty, & bumpy house, groovy, jacking techno, lush deep house, & the raw, rhythmic power of UK bass & breaks. Currently delving into production, remixing Welly talent, & crafting his own releases, PocketLipps is a DJ who lives for the shared boogie, always found flailing wildly alongside the crowd.

id: Butch Auction-level 1/60 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Butch Auction
venue: level 1/60 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

Venue is wheelchair accessible with lift access and accessible bathrooms.

id: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connections, Reflections and Possibilities-Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connections, Reflections and Possibilities
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Come and join Te Whiri Whītau as we celebrate a year of learning, making, connecting and dreaming together.

We warmly invite you to join in conversation, connection and celebration as we reflect on the year that has been and share our aspirations for the future. This gathering is an opportunity to learn more about the work of Te Whiri Whītau, hear about current and emerging research, meet our researchers and collaborators, and explore opportunities for collaboration, partnership, creative practice and research.

Over the course of the event, we'll share research highlights, introduce our new visual identity, and open conversations about the role that fibres, textiles and materials can play in creating thriving communities, cultures, environments and economies.

Whether you are a researcher, practitioner, student, industry partner, community organisation or supporter of our work, we would love you to join us as we strengthen connections, celebrate achievements, and look ahead to what's possible together.

Light refreshments will be served.

long_description:
Practice a VocalVinyasa class that will enliven your body. Science shows that sound vibrations, especially those from our voices, create physiological benefits that balance the body and mind.

Yoga Voice is a form of yoga combining specific vocal tones to tune into the body as a sounding and breathing apparatus. These classes are ideal for anyone who uses their voice and wants to keep their body and voice in optimal health, it can be especially beneficial for singers, actors, performers, yoga practitioners, teachers and musicians.

Cost:

Casual class $20.00

4 classes for the price of 3 $60.00 book before 1st Nov.

Student/Unwaged $10.00

Your Teacher:

Sascha Perfect (RYT 200 RYVT250)

Sascha is a qualified yoga teacher and performer. She has a RYT 200 accreditation from Hot Yoga Wellington, a RYVT 250 with Yoga Voice and is currently training to be a Soul Voice practitioner. Her yoga journey began in Ireland and she has trained with voice and somatic practitioners in Europe including Frank Van De Ven, Tadashi Endo, Enrique Pardo, Anne Marie Blink, Karina Schelde and traditional Vedic chanting with Menaka Desikachar.

id: Dungeons & Dragons - An All Ages Adventure-28 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Dungeons & Dragons - An All Ages Adventure
venue: 28 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand
long_description:
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

long_description:
Join us for an evening of networking and inspiration with other young professionals in the infrastructure industry. The theme for this year's Networking for the Future event is 'The Future of Construction: What Will Our Jobs Look Like?’.

The evening will include drinks, nibbles, and a panel Q&A session featuring:

Andrew Mcleod - Wellington Transport & Water Manager from AECOM

Beth Parkin - Business Leader, Water, Lower North Island from Stantec

Will Watkins - Mechanical Building Services Technical Director from Aurecon

Michael Howden - Digital Services & Innovation

As digital tools, automation, and AI reshape the infrastructure sector, understanding what skills and mindsets will be needed for the future is becoming more essential than ever for early professionals. For those of us in the early stages of our careers, understanding how these changes may affect future opportunities and skill requirements has never been more important.

Join AECOM’s annual event as industry leaders share insights on the future of infrastructure through a panel discussion and Q&A, followed by networking with Wellington’s emerging professionals. Connect, learn, and gain valuable perspectives on the industry ahead.

Get ready to hear more about the infrastructure industry and connect with other early infrastructure professionals.

Tickets for this event are free for early professionals.

Please come prepared with questions for our panelists!

EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

venue: 41-47 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
‘Oneiric Reality | The architecture of a dream’ is what it feels like to live between two worlds: the one you come from and the one you’ve built. Some of it feels like a dream, some of it feels like home, and some of it feels like both at once. For three days, both live in the same room.


A kind of lucid dream: knowing you’re inside it, and discovering you can choose what comes next.

Work by Latin American artists and artists of Latin heritage from across Aotearoa: paint, ink, photographs, collage, poems. Not all of it is dreamlike. All of it was made from somewhere in between.

Fri 27 Nov: opening night, 7:30 pm

Sat 28 Nov: 11 am to 2 pm and 5 pm to 8 pm

Sun 29 Nov: 12 pm to 3 pm

Come as you are. Wander in any direction.

name: Free Women's Self Defence Course
venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

name: The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

Join us for Aotearoa's first Indigenous Tech Summit. Two packed days of keynotes and kōrero from indigenous innovators across the globe and Aotearoa.

For centuries, the vast expanse of Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa was not a barrier separating our people. It was the original superhighway, connecting Indigenous navigators, traders and innovators across the Pacific.

The Indigenous Tech Summit 2026 reclaims this narrative.

Led by ancestral wisdom and cutting-edge digital capability, the summit brings together Māori and global Indigenous tech communities to navigate the future of artificial intelligence, data sovereignty, enterprise and workforce development.

We invite you to join us as we navigate these new realms.

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40, reduced to $20 for those with a Community Services Card, fully refundable until one day prior.

Hailing from Italy and now rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister quickly burst onto Aotearoa’s dance floors and has been on a rapid rise ever since. She’s lit up festivals like Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and Arkadien and supported international acts including KC Lights.
She currently holds a radio residency on Wellington’s iconic Radio Active, where her show dives deep into house and underground sounds.

After being missing for 14 years, he was ‘liberated’ by the Red Cross in Northern Africa ‘working’ on an Ethiopian pirate ship in the Gulf of Aden.
He was in desperate need of revitalisation, so was moved to their base deep in the Amazon basin, in Peru, near the border of Brazil, where he was healed by Amazonian Shamans using an ancient technique.

id: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

Film Adjacent presents Intimate Earth, a symposium dedicated to the aesthetic, cultural and political energies of experimental film in Aotearoa and beyond. Intimate Earth celebrates ways of seeing in distinction to dominant modes of audio-visual media in the twenty-first century. The symposium will assemble artists, curators and audiences around micro and macrocosmic imaginations of a world otherwise. 

This will be a two-day event, featuring six programmes, multiple roundtable discussions, and a filmmaking workshop. Attendees can come and go as they please.

6:30pm - 8:30pm: Electromorphic Poetry. Pres. by Tyler Shane Tesolin + video introduction by R. Bruce Elder

long_description:
Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

Venue is wheelchair accessible with lift access and accessible bathrooms.

Immerse yourself in a breathtaking 3-hour cinematic journey into the world’s most spectacular marine environments. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour brings together an extraordinary collection of short films celebrating the beauty, power and wonder of our oceans.

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. Meet the passionate divers, fearless surfers, dedicated ocean advocates, ocean explorers and marine scientists whose lives are shaped by their connection to the sea.

Featuring spectacular underwater cinematography, heart-stopping ocean adventures and intimate stories of the people who dedicate their lives to exploring and protecting our oceans, every film offers a fresh perspective on the world beneath the waves.

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.

The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power. Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

id: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Special guest: Joe Cole

long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

When effective presenters speak, they do more than inform - they influence, persuade, and inspire. That isn’t down to magic or your personality; it’s method. With the right tools, anyone can build genuine connection and move a room.

This workshop is for leaders, emerging leaders, technical specialists, and professionals who want practical tools and techniques for speaking in both formal and informal settings.

Short on time? Attend 1 Day (Foundations) for all the core skills. Ready for a bigger shift? Choose 2 Days (Advanced) for one on one coaching and deeper transformation. Pick what’s right for you.

Small group format for maximum practice and feedback (no massive groups).

Plan engaging content (fast)

Plan faster, make better decisions about what to include (and what to ditch).

 

Design useful slides (not wallpaper)

A simple but revolutionary way to design slides that support - not sabotage - your message.

Practical guidance on using AI to fast-track draft slides and create supporting documents (and how to avoid creating AI slop!)

How to use PowerPoint to keep you on track without putting your audience to sleep.

 

Keep nerves under control

A proven psychological approach to calm the mental chatter that causes waffling, speed talking, and blank moments.

Build a personal plan to shift focus from “me” to the audience and the outcome you want.

 

Deliver in a natural, engaging way

Three delivery techniques that help you look credible, be engaging and feel confident.

If you’re ready for lasting, transformative change in your communication skills, the two-day option is the best choice.

Everything from Day 1 (Foundations) PLUS

Go deeper with planning

A practical way to prepare when time is tight — so you own your words.

One-on-one coaching targeted to your specific needs.

Strategies for side chats, interruptions, distractions, disagreement, and the odd angry voice - while staying calm and in control.

long_description:
We warmly invite you to this BWB Talk with Aroha Harris to celebrate the publication of her new book, We Are What We Write.

Aroha Harris (Te Rarawa, Ngāpuhi) MNZM is an award-winning historian and Associate Professor of History at Waipapa Taumata Rau–the University of Auckland. In this wide-ranging collection of essays, she brings together more than two decades of writing, drawing from public lectures, essays, tributes and previously unpublished reflections. Written with characteristic warmth and intellectual clarity, the collection explores the tensions between policy and people, the reshaping of Māori-Crown relationships, and the everyday acts of remembering that shape Māori worlds.

Please join us at the National Library | Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa for this event with Aroha Harris.

name: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Home Alone Music is proud to announce the Aotearoa and Australian tour in celebration of Timothy Blackman's new album 'Between the Islands' (HAM050) in January/February 2027.  

In Aotearoa, there will be full band shows in Wellington and Palmerston North. 

For the full band shows, Timothy's backing band will consist of Tessa Dillion on bass/backing vocals (Mystery Waitress and Tessa de Lyon) and Olivia Campion on drums (Mystery Waitress and Yumi Zouma).

Between the Islands was recorded with a live studio band consisting of Blackman, Tessa Dillon (Mystery Waitress), and Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (French for Rabbits, Dateline). Lee Prebble recorded and mixed their performances at The Surgery Recording Studio in Omāroro, Newtown, Wellington over three days in May 2025. Additional overdubs were performed and recorded by Blackman’s longtime collaborator Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) at her home in Wellington. The album was mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago, Illinois.  Album artwork by Alex Thornton.  


----

Timothy Blackman is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington based singer-songwriter, recording artist and founder of independent Aotearoa New Zealand record label Home Alone.

Since his first EP in 2006, Blackman has released a string of acclaimed records such as Modern Sprawl, I've Never Lived, Everyone Needs Something to Hold On To and Brightest Days. Blackman grew up in the Wellington region, began playing violin at five and guitar at ten, and was performing in bands around the Lower Hutt/Wellington area as a teenager. 

His music has since taken him from the bedrooms and small venues of Aotearoa to stages across Europe, the UK, United States and Australia, where he has performed alongside artists including The Mountain Goats and Scout Niblett. His music sits in an intimate space, flitting somewhere between the introspective songwriting of Bill Callahan and Bonnie Prince Billy, and the DIY spirit of New Zealand icon Chris Knox. His songs are personal and unvarnished: thoughtful, melancholic and often quietly funny, with a fascination for place, memory, displacement and the strange details of everyday life.

embroidery with beads workshop: Slow Down. Make something.

Join me for a cozy, beginner-friendly embroidery workshop designed for adults who want to learn something new and enjoy a creative evening together.

This workshop is all about slowing down, crafting together, and enjoying the process in a relaxed, welcoming space.

All materials are provided, and you’ll head home with:

A piece of practice fabric + a blank square for your next project

An embroidery hoop, needle, some thread and the fabric you need to finish your project



Soft drinks (hot and cold) and snacks will also be available to keep our creative energy flowing.

Please note, the workshop will be cancelled if less than 3 participants are signed up 7 days prior to the date.

For the first time in 10 years - Mark Moroney & David Shanhun are reuniting for a series of intimate shows across New Zealand in 2026. This special tour brings their signature blend of world-class guitar playing, heartfelt songwriting, rich harmonies, and light-hearted banter back to audiences around the country. Expect an evening of unforgettable music, plenty of laughs, and the kind of connection that only comes from two great friends & musicians sharing the stage.

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

"Once in a while you see an artist who is out of the ordinary." - The Shirley Ryder Show

David Shanhun has opened for Rock legends Foreigner, & Heart, and has performed in NZ, Japan, Australia, and the UK. His exquisite guitar work shines under his superb storytelling and songwriting. He's performed with Grammy Award winner Bryan White, and is known for his engaging live shows and heartfelt tunes.

long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

venue: 28 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand
long_description:
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

long_description:
🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

📅 Event details

Date: Saturday 28 November 2026

Time: 1:00–3:00 PM

Location: Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub

Address: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington

Cost: FREE

Spaces: Limited to 25 registrations

📱 What to bring

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

A free AI chatbot app, if you already have one

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

Don't have an AI app? No worries! You can follow the live demonstrations or work with a partner.

💛 Why we're doing this

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

🎟️ Reserve your FREE place today.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with venue support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

Please note: This is a practical learning workshop, not a formal IELTS assessment or band-scoring session.
