name: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Advanced

The Advanced workshop is for musicians who already have some experience with improvisation and jazz playing, or players with more advanced technique looking to dive deeper into the language of jazz.

Participants will take an in-depth look at playing jazz standards with the rhythm section, explore different styles and traditions, develop listening skills, and gain musical insights from the professional musicians leading the workshop.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

name: The Muppet Christmas Carol - booking
venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

long_description:
Christmas Fantasia

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul, 2 Hill Street, Thorndon


General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

School-aged children free


Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

id: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

James Fuller, Co-Founder at HNRY

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.




	

James Fuller; Co-founder at HNRY

	

James Fuller began his career as an application developer, before moving into technology strategy and consultancy. After senior roles at Thomson Reuters and Deloitte, he decided to strike out on his own as a growth consultant for startup, corporate, and government clients.

It was rewarding work, but James found himself struggling with the amount of tax and financial admin involved in being self-employed. To solve the issue, he and co-founder Claire created a simple, homemade system to automate calculating and paying self-employed taxes.

They shared their system with self-employed friends, realised that there was a market for it, and got to work improving their solution .In 2017, James and Claire officially launched Hnry; a service designed to automatically calculate, pay, and file taxes for sole traders.

Today, Hnry is New Zealand’s largest, and Australasia’s fastest-growing accounting service. We process billions of dollars worth of payments every year, handling around 1% of New Zealand’s tax revenue.

Best of all, we free up thousands of hours for clients to focus more on what they do best - their jobs. Hnry is on a mission to make self-employment simple, affordable, and accessible for anyone.

long_description:
embroidery with beads workshop: Slow Down. Make something.

Join me for a cozy, beginner-friendly embroidery workshop designed for adults who want to learn something new and enjoy a creative evening together.

In this 2hour session, I’ll guide you through the basic stitches you need to get started with hand embroidery and help you start your own project on your item of clothing.

We’ll begin by practicing on small fabric squares so you can build confidence and get comfortable with your needle and thread, practice how to attach beads before starting a project onto a piece of clothing you’ve brought along or a piece of fabric from my stash — turning it into something beautifully personal and unique.

This workshop is all about slowing down, crafting together, and enjoying the process in a relaxed, welcoming space.

All materials are provided, and you’ll head home with:

A piece of practice fabric + a blank square for your next project

An embroidery hoop, needle, some thread and the fabric you need to finish your project



Soft drinks (hot and cold) and snacks will also be available to keep our creative energy flowing.

No experience is needed — just bring an item of clothing you’d love to transform (or a bag, a pouch, anything you can stitch on) and a willingness to try something new. I can’t wait to stitch with you 🤍

Please note, the workshop will be cancelled if less than 3 participants are signed up 7 days prior to the date.

long_description:
The iconic bluesman and one of Australia’s most revered live performers, Lloyd Spiegel, brings his world-famous guitar work, soulful voice, and deeply human storytelling to New Zealand in April 2027!

This is a rare chance to experience world-class artistry up close, in an intimate listening-room setting designed for focus, connection, and a true love of live music.

“A guitarist almost without peer, Spiegel deconstructs how the blues guitar is supposed to operate… makes sweet love to it, then kicks it out the back door.” — Australian Guitar Player

“Spiegel is ALL presence, authority, rhythm and drive. He epitomizes control, soul and passion with white-hot ferocity and blazing instrumental mastery.” — The Age (Melbourne)

📍 Friday 17 April 2027 @ Old St Paul's - Wellington

Seated concert

Doors 7 PM | Show 7:30 PM

Family friendly, with discounted tickets for under 18s

DON'T miss your chance to experience live music at its finest!

ABOUT LLOYD SPIEGEL

Lloyd Spiegel is a travelling bluesman at heart — a guitarist by trade and a storyteller by nature. The 14-time Australian Blues Award winner has spent a lifetime refining a signature style that honours the deep traditions of blues while pushing the music forward in his own unmistakable voice.

His performances move effortlessly between jaw-dropping guitar work, powerful vocals, humour, and deeply human moments, creating shows that feel personal, generous, and completely alive in the room.

With ten albums to his name and an international touring career spanning North America, Europe, Japan, and beyond, Lloyd is equally respected on world-class festival stages and in intimate listening rooms. At home in Australia, he is recognised as a trailblazer for blues music and has been named among the 50 greatest Australian guitarists of all time.

Whether playing to thousands or a quiet, attentive audience, Lloyd Spiegel has a rare gift for connection — making every performance feel like a shared experience, and every listener feel part of the story.

ABOUT THE VENUE

Located in the heart of Wellington, the magnificent Old St Paul’s is one of New Zealand’s most beautiful historic churches, renowned for its stunning timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and warm, intimate atmosphere.

For one special night, Nightingale Concerts transforms this breathtaking heritage landmark into a listening room, bringing audiences together to experience the extraordinary musicianship, stories, and energy of Lloyd Spiegel up close.

Expect an evening of remarkable guitar playing, powerful blues, laughter, and the kind of connection that makes live music so special.

🎟️ Tickets are ON SALE NOW! These intimate concerts have been selling out in venues around the world. With limited seating available, don't miss your chance to experience Lloyd Spiegel live in Wellington!

long_description:
🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

📅 Event details

Date: Saturday 28 November 2026

Time: 1:00–3:00 PM

Location: Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub

Address: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington

Cost: FREE

Spaces: Limited to 25 registrations

📱 What to bring

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

A free AI chatbot app, if you already have one

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

Don't have an AI app? No worries! You can follow the live demonstrations or work with a partner.

💛 Why we're doing this

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

🎟️ Reserve your FREE place today.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with venue support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

Please note: This is a practical learning workshop, not a formal IELTS assessment or band-scoring session.

An afternoon of exploratory improvisations and new compositions at Karori's Futuna Chapel. Doors open at 2pm, music starts 2:30pm.



Doxing Ur Mum is a new song cycle composed by Mallory Elmo, with lyrics by poet and textile artist Anne Amber, performed by Kassandra Wang (mezzo-soprano) and Antonia Grant (violin). 

The fruit of three years of collaboration, these songs speak aphoristically of everyday, intimate, and queer personal experiences in the city of Pōneke. Kassandra and Antonia will also perform a new work by Ōtautahi-based composer Luka Reardon and a collaborative composition of their own.



Multifaceted musicians lucky pollock, Amy-Jane, and Tristan Carter will join forces on flute, violin, keyboard, and more, exploring ambient free improvisation through their shared classical, popular, and experimental backgrounds. 

scramble204, Shay Patel (guitar)'s project with Vinnie Whitehead (guitar) and Alex Hoare (cello), will present an iteration of their Dialogues series.



Presented by Swamp Soul and Pyramid Club Offsite

long_description:
YOUR VOICE. YOUR CONFIDENCE. YOUR FUTURE.

What could you achieve if you were a more confident communicator?

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

James Fuller, Co-Founder at HNRY

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.




	

James Fuller; Co-founder at HNRY

	

James Fuller began his career as an application developer, before moving into technology strategy and consultancy. After senior roles at Thomson Reuters and Deloitte, he decided to strike out on his own as a growth consultant for startup, corporate, and government clients.

It was rewarding work, but James found himself struggling with the amount of tax and financial admin involved in being self-employed. To solve the issue, he and co-founder Claire created a simple, homemade system to automate calculating and paying self-employed taxes.

They shared their system with self-employed friends, realised that there was a market for it, and got to work improving their solution .In 2017, James and Claire officially launched Hnry; a service designed to automatically calculate, pay, and file taxes for sole traders.

Today, Hnry is New Zealand’s largest, and Australasia’s fastest-growing accounting service. We process billions of dollars worth of payments every year, handling around 1% of New Zealand’s tax revenue.

Best of all, we free up thousands of hours for clients to focus more on what they do best - their jobs. Hnry is on a mission to make self-employment simple, affordable, and accessible for anyone.

venue: 52/70 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Handstands and getting upside down are good for our upper body, core strength, confidence, resilience and overall body knowledge. 

This workshop is an opportunity to learn the steps towards stable handstands within a safe environment.  This workshop is designed for folks who have interest in and maybe some experience with handstands who are keen to learn the alignment and ways to practice building up to holding them. What a better way to welcome summer than with a new trick to practice on the lawn! 


Workshop will cover:
- falling safely

- exercises to warm up and build upper body, forearm, hand strength

- the biomechanics and alignment of hand balancing

- safe ways to practice handstands at your level

- hands-on assistance

- personal feedback and tips


Your facilitators:JJ Simmons

JJ started standing on her hands about the same time as on her feet. In the past 15 yrs since training in Gymnastics and Physical Education in Denmark and Yoga teacher training, JJ has seen many adults of all abilities (hand)STAND STRONG. She's known for her experience, dynamism and care, and would love to have you join. 

Porou Wise

Porou has been involved in the health and fitness industry for over a decade. Porou’s specialty is in strength and hypertrophy condition training, body composition, general mobility work and boxing. In his spare time, Porou can be found working on his own physique in the gym, out walking with his two British bulldogs, Awhi and Uno.

PARTICIPANTS NEED

basic upperbody stregnth (can hold a plank/prone position)

readiness to try being upside down

name: Larval Mask - Physical Theatre Workshops
venue: 3 Market Lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40, reduced to $20 for those with a Community Services Card, fully refundable until one day prior.

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

An afternoon of exploratory improvisations and new compositions at Karori's Futuna Chapel. Doors open at 2pm, music starts 2:30pm.



Doxing Ur Mum is a new song cycle composed by Mallory Elmo, with lyrics by poet and textile artist Anne Amber, performed by Kassandra Wang (mezzo-soprano) and Antonia Grant (violin). 

The fruit of three years of collaboration, these songs speak aphoristically of everyday, intimate, and queer personal experiences in the city of Pōneke. Kassandra and Antonia will also perform a new work by Ōtautahi-based composer Luka Reardon and a collaborative composition of their own.



Multifaceted musicians lucky pollock, Amy-Jane, and Tristan Carter will join forces on flute, violin, keyboard, and more, exploring ambient free improvisation through their shared classical, popular, and experimental backgrounds. 

scramble204, Shay Patel (guitar)'s project with Vinnie Whitehead (guitar) and Alex Hoare (cello), will present an iteration of their Dialogues series.



Presented by Swamp Soul and Pyramid Club Offsite

Poster design by Shay Patel

id: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)-311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)
venue: 311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Living with ADHD can be tiring. Constantly trying harder.

Wondering why things that seem simple for other people can feel so difficult.

Liminal is a workshop designed to help make sense of that experience — and to help you discover practical ways forward.

This isn’t about fixing yourself. It’s about working with how you’re wired.

You’ll leave with:

a clearer understanding of why your ADHD works the way it does

practical strategies you can begin using immediately

hope that life can become easier

Rather than leaving with another list of things you "should" do, you'll leave with one or two small experiments that fit your own life.

What we'll explore

ADHD: why it works the way it does, and why life can feel so much harder than it should.

Emotional regulation: sometimes one of the most overlooked parts of ADHD.

Executive functioning: why starting, planning, remembering, and following through can be so difficult.

Dopamine: motivation, energy, and why "just try harder" rarely works.

Tiny Habits®: a simple, practical way to begin making lasting changes.

Liminal offers education and practical support; it doesn’t replace professional care, provide diagnosis or offer advice about medication.

Who is this for?

This workshop is best suited to adults (16+) who already have some understanding of ADHD — whether diagnosed, self-identified, exploring or supporting someone in your whanau.

However, anyone is welcome.

Come as you are.
You don't need to have everything sorted.
Just bring your curiosity.

Details at a glance

Date: Saturday 28th November 2026

Venue: St Hilda's Church, 11 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington

Time:

10.00am - Registration, coffee, snacks

10.15am - Workshop begins

12.30ish. Light lunch (included)

2.30pm - Finish

What’s included

Coffee and snacks, light lunch

Workbook materials (new and revamped; including an experiment guide)

A chance to reflect, connect, and further develop your own individual plan

Cost

Individual: $70

Couple: $110

Multiple: Two from one family/whanau: $110

For unwaged tickets ($40) or larger family groups please contact Derek on 021 511 303. You can get an access code to for a group discount.

Some sponsored (free) places are available.

Register by

Please register by the Thursday prior (26th November).

If are signing up . . .

If you have any questions, any information it may be helpful for me to know or requests, please call,

Presenter: Derek Chirnside

Over the past twenty years I've listened to many of adults describe what ADHD feels like from the inside. Again and again I hear similar themes: feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, shamed, huge creativity, humour, resilience, and the longing to simply make life work a little better. Also, timeblindness and hyperfocus!

This workshop grew out of those conversations.

I'm based in Christchurch. I've worked as a classroom teacher, teacher educator (including training teachers to support students with ADHD), university chaplain, and business owner. I'm a long-time ADHD educator with a particular focus on practical, sustainable strategies that help adults live well with ADHD. More information on website

Learningworkshops.nz

venue: Level 5/39 Webb Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Unsung Heroes!

Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley -with special guest Angela Fox- share songs, stories and a slideshow from NZ's distant past. Together, they bring to life the characters and stories of our past - the quirky and macabre - that shaped who we are today.

Chris Priestley is a singer, songwriter & NZ historian. He has recorded eight albums and his musical spans over 40 years. As a hospitality entrepreneur he was co-founder of Real Groovy Records & café/music venues Java Jive, Kerouacs, Atomic and Café One2One in Ponsonby.

Cameron Bennett is a storyteller, singer songwriter and plays guitar and lap steel guitar. Journalism is his day job - he currently produces a weekly tv current affairs programme and is director/writer of the ongoing NZ Land Wars documentaries. New Zealand colonial history is in his blood; from the Wairau Affray to the Western Front, his forebears have borne witness - miners, gamblers, union organisers, shopkeepers and servicemen.

name: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)
venue: 311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Living with ADHD can be tiring. Constantly trying harder.

Wondering why things that seem simple for other people can feel so difficult.

Liminal is a workshop designed to help make sense of that experience — and to help you discover practical ways forward.

This isn’t about fixing yourself. It’s about working with how you’re wired.

You’ll leave with:

a clearer understanding of why your ADHD works the way it does

practical strategies you can begin using immediately

hope that life can become easier

Rather than leaving with another list of things you "should" do, you'll leave with one or two small experiments that fit your own life.

What we'll explore

ADHD: why it works the way it does, and why life can feel so much harder than it should.

Emotional regulation: sometimes one of the most overlooked parts of ADHD.

Executive functioning: why starting, planning, remembering, and following through can be so difficult.

Dopamine: motivation, energy, and why "just try harder" rarely works.

Tiny Habits®: a simple, practical way to begin making lasting changes.

Liminal offers education and practical support; it doesn’t replace professional care, provide diagnosis or offer advice about medication.

Who is this for?

This workshop is best suited to adults (16+) who already have some understanding of ADHD — whether diagnosed, self-identified, exploring or supporting someone in your whanau.

However, anyone is welcome.

Come as you are.
You don't need to have everything sorted.
Just bring your curiosity.

Details at a glance

Date: Saturday 28th November 2026

Venue: St Hilda's Church, 11 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington

Time:

10.00am - Registration, coffee, snacks

10.15am - Workshop begins

For unwaged tickets ($40) or larger family groups please contact Derek on 021 511 303. You can get an access code to for a group discount.

Some sponsored (free) places are available.

Register by

Please register by the Thursday prior (26th November).

If are signing up . . .

If you have any questions, any information it may be helpful for me to know or requests, please call,

Presenter: Derek Chirnside

Over the past twenty years I've listened to many of adults describe what ADHD feels like from the inside. Again and again I hear similar themes: feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, shamed, huge creativity, humour, resilience, and the longing to simply make life work a little better. Also, timeblindness and hyperfocus!

This workshop grew out of those conversations.

I'm based in Christchurch. I've worked as a classroom teacher, teacher educator (including training teachers to support students with ADHD), university chaplain, and business owner. I'm a long-time ADHD educator with a particular focus on practical, sustainable strategies that help adults live well with ADHD. More information on website

Learningworkshops.nz

id: Beyond the BIM-65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Beyond the BIM
venue: 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Election periods can be strange times in the public sector.

Uncertainty, relief, frustration, hope, grief, curiosity, exhaustion, or a mix of all of them before the second cup of coffee. Most of us keep moving because the work still needs doing. That doesn't leave much room to notice what's happening beneath the surface.

Are you a public servant navigating change, uncertainty, and the twelfth rewrite of the BIM?

Beyond the BIM is a chance to step away from your desk for 45 minutes. Get some of what you’re carrying out of your head and onto paper, so you walk back with a bit more room than you left with.

You'll receive a small sketchbook to keep, along with a handful of reflective prompts and access to a table full of stickers, pens, pencils and washi tape.

Whether you've been wrestling with 3am ruminations, gone cross-eyed from staring at your screen, or simply need to trade the office air-con for a different flavour of recycled air, you're welcome here. Bring a colleague if you’d rather not walk in alone.

This is a space totally unconcerned with politics and fully concerned with people.

We'll spend a little time noticing, creating and exploring. There will be an opportunity to share at the end if you'd like to, but you're equally welcome to keep your reflections entirely to yourself.

This session is offered on a koha basis. Contributions towards venue hire and materials are welcome, but not expected.

Come as you are.

long_description:
32nd New Zealand Microscopy Conference

Under the theme “Shaping the Future of Microscopy in Aotearoa New Zealand”, we warmly invite everyone involved in microscopy and microanalysis to attend our annual meeting.

This year, the conference will be held at the Pipitea Campus, Victoria University of Wellington, from 24-27 November 2026.

The conference aims to showcase advances in microscopy and microanalysis developed in New Zealand, covering a wide range of fields including biotechnology, materials science, environmental science, image analysis, artificial intelligence, data management, and homegrown technologies.

In addition, the programme will feature special interest workshops, including image analysis using QuPath, facility management, and a technology showcase.

Don’t miss out—register now!

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

long_description:

We warmly invite you to join in conversation, connection and celebration as we reflect on the year that has been and share our aspirations for the future. This gathering is an opportunity to learn more about the work of Te Whiri Whītau, hear about current and emerging research, meet our researchers and collaborators, and explore opportunities for collaboration, partnership, creative practice and research.

id: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

long_description:
Te Whanganui-a-Tara's Half/Angel will play the Newtown Barrel Brothers on November 20th to round off 2026. Joined by Wear Pounamu, Venus Mae, and Jjoyce, three must see Wellington acts, this is not a show to miss out on.

Half/Angel are one of the most exciting acts emerging from Te Whanganui-a-Tara right now. Toeing the lines of alt-rock, psychedelia, and indie, Half/Angel juxtapose intimate, soft vocals and delicate instrumental passages with explosive high-energy passages.

Joined by JJoyce: Wellington Band, Est. 2025.

JJoyce are an alternative/experimental rock band whose enigmatic presence keeps their audience on their toes. The JJoyce live experience is always an action packed and captivating time worth every dollar.

Venus Mae: 'I’m venus mae and I make music from Wellington New Zealand. Make yourself at home'

Ethereal, self produced folktronica artist Venus Mae is one of Wellington's hidden indie gems. This will be her second live appearance to date.

Venus Mae's second EP, 'Apple Of MY Eye' is out now.

And Wear Pounamu:

Wear Pounamu is a Whanganui-born experimental DJ and producer residing in Pōneke. They have opened for an eclectic range of artists, including James K, Mokotron, and Tom Scott..

Half/Angel are incredibly excited to announce our first headline show of 2026. If you've been waiting to see us play this year, this is the show. Come and join us for a night of community, friends, and music.

name: Free Women's Self Defence Course
venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

id: Shaping streets that put people first-139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaping streets that put people first
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

name: Beyond the BIM
venue: 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Election periods can be strange times in the public sector.

Uncertainty, relief, frustration, hope, grief, curiosity, exhaustion, or a mix of all of them before the second cup of coffee. Most of us keep moving because the work still needs doing. That doesn't leave much room to notice what's happening beneath the surface.

Are you a public servant navigating change, uncertainty, and the twelfth rewrite of the BIM?

Beyond the BIM is a chance to step away from your desk for 45 minutes. Get some of what you’re carrying out of your head and onto paper, so you walk back with a bit more room than you left with.

You'll receive a small sketchbook to keep, along with a handful of reflective prompts and access to a table full of stickers, pens, pencils and washi tape.

Whether you've been wrestling with 3am ruminations, gone cross-eyed from staring at your screen, or simply need to trade the office air-con for a different flavour of recycled air, you're welcome here. Bring a colleague if you’d rather not walk in alone.

This is a space totally unconcerned with politics and fully concerned with people.

We'll spend a little time noticing, creating and exploring. There will be an opportunity to share at the end if you'd like to, but you're equally welcome to keep your reflections entirely to yourself.

This session is offered on a koha basis. Contributions towards venue hire and materials are welcome, but not expected.

Come as you are.

id: Quiz night Wednesday: Fundraiser for Tim-163 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Quiz night Wednesday: Fundraiser for Tim
venue: 163 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
For one night only DUB HUB’s Quiz Night Wednesday is becoming a fundraiser for Tim Cox.

Tim is a dad, husband, brother and friend from Island Bay who is living with incurable pancreatic cancer. Your support has already helped him get to the USA for life-extending treatment. The costs were well over what was raised so we’re keeping the support going to help cover the remaining expenses and look after his family.

Tim, along with a bunch of other Dads, has been on a quiz team at the Island Bay pub most weeks for about 12 years. It started as a playdate set up by the Mums when the kids were all at playcentre together, and the 'Dads team' has ebbed and flowed ever since.

So on 25 November, grab your friends, form a team (or come solo and we’ll place you on one) join alongside the 'Dad's team' and test your general knowledge. Every $10 ticket goes to Tim and his family.

Buy tickets for your whole team in one go, or have each person buy their own.

When purchasing your ticket you’ll be asked to supply a team captain name, This will assist us to allocate tables. If you don’t have a team yet, just let us know when booking and we’ll sort you out.

$10 a ticket,
8 people maximum per team.
Quit starts at 7pm, but please arrive earlier to get settled.

Can’t make it? You can still donate at givealittle.co.nz/cause/help-tim-get-life-extending-treatment

Thank you to the DUB HUB team for their support and for allowing us to takeover Quiz Night Wednesday.

id: Young Photographer Awards 2026-2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

Hear from practitioners across both disciplines as they share a glimpse into their day-to-day work, the challenges they tackle, and the approaches to tackling behaviour change challenges.

Please RSVP so we can keep track of numbers, feel free to invite others that are interested in behaviour change.

CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event.
